etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English coveten, coveiten, coveyten, from Old French covoitier (modern French convoiter), from covoitié (“desire”), presumably modified from Latin cupiditas.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To wish for with eagerness; to desire possession of, often enviously.

quote.citation: 1991, Ted Tally, The Silence of the Lambs (motion picture), spoken by Hannibal Lecter (Anthony Hopkins):
quote.text: No! He covets. That is his nature. And how do we begin to covet, Clarice? Do we seek out things to covet? Make an effort to answer now.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To long for inordinately or unlawfully; to hanker after (something forbidden).
(intransitive) To yearn; to have or indulge an inordinate desire, especially for another's possession.
